subject: maths
title: Primary 6 Ratio Word Problems
seo_title: P6 Ratio Word Problems Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE)
meta_desc: Free P6 ratio word problems: sharing, difference given, before-and-after and 3-part ratios with bar models. 100 PSLE-style questions with answers.
key_big: Change the ratio into units, find 1 unit, then multiply.
key_sub: Ratio 3 : 5 and Siti has $24 more: 2 units = $24, so 1 unit = $12 and Ali has 3 × $12 = $36.
body_html:
Units: the key to every ratio problem

A ratio tells you how many equal units each person has. In 2 : 3, the first person has 2 units and the second has 3 units. Every unit has the same value.

The plan is always the same: find what 1 unit is worth, then multiply.

Sharing a total

Ali and Siti share $60 in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does each get?

2 + 3 = 5 units. 5 units = $60, so 1 unit = $12. Ali: 2 × $12 = $24. Siti: 3 × $12 = $36.

Answer: Ali $24, Siti $36

When one part or the difference is given

Match the number you know with the right number of units.

Difference given

The ratio of Ali’s money to Siti’s money is 3 : 5. Siti has $24 more than Ali. How much does Ali have?

The difference is 5 − 3 = 2 units. 2 units = $24, so 1 unit = $12. Ali: 3 × $12 = $36.

Answer: $36

Before and after

First ask: what stays the same? Then make its units the same in both ratios.

What happensWhat stays the sameMake the same
One person buys, spends or gives awayThe other person’s amountThat person’s units
One person gives some to the otherThe totalThe total units
Both get older, or both spend the same amountThe differenceThe difference in units
One quantity unchanged

The ratio of Ahmad’s stickers to Mei Ling’s stickers was 3 : 4. Ahmad bought 16 more stickers and the ratio became 5 : 4. How many stickers does Mei Ling have?

Mei Ling’s stickers do not change, and she has 4 units in both ratios. Ahmad went from 3 units to 5 units, so 2 units = 16 and 1 unit = 8. Mei Ling: 4 × 8 = 32.

Answer: 32 stickers

Total unchanged

The ratio of Wei Ming’s marbles to Hui Min’s marbles was 3 : 1. Wei Ming gave Hui Min 10 marbles. Then they had the same number. How many marbles did Wei Ming have at first?

The total stays 4 units, so after they have 2 units each. Wei Ming gave 3 − 2 = 1 unit = 10. At first: 3 × 10 = 30.

Answer: 30 marbles

If the units do not match, change one ratio first. For 2 : 3 before and 1 : 2 after, with the first amount unchanged, write 1 : 2 as 2 : 4.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Sharing $60 in 2 : 3 by working out $60 ÷ 2 or $60 ÷ 3Add the units first: 5 units = $60, so 1 unit = $12
Treating the difference as 1 unit: “Siti has $24 more” so 1 unit = $24Count the units in the difference: 5 − 3 = 2 units = $24
Changing the amount that stays the sameFind what does not change and give it the same units in both ratios
Comparing 5 : 3 and 1 : 3 directly when the total stays the sameThe totals are 8 and 4 units. Write 1 : 3 as 2 : 6 first
Joining 2 : 3 and 4 : 5 into 2 : 3 : 5Make the shared amount the same: 8 : 12 and 12 : 15 give 8 : 12 : 15

faq.q: How do you solve ratio word problems in P6?
faq.a: Turn the ratio into units, find what 1 unit is worth, then multiply. For $60 shared in the ratio 2 : 3, 5 units = $60, so 1 unit = $12 and the shares are $24 and $36.

They are problems where an amount changes and the ratio changes with it. Find what stays the same (one person’s amount, the total or the difference), give it the same number of units in both ratios, then compare.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in ratio word problems?
faq.a: Treating a given difference or total as 1 unit. If Siti has $24 more and the ratio is 3 : 5, the $24 is 2 units, so 1 unit is $12.

faq.q: Is ratio tested in the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. Ratio is part of the MOE Primary 6 syllabus, and PSLE Paper 2 often has multi-step ratio problems, including before-and-after and three-part ratios, that are best solved with bar models.

sets.title: Sharing a total in a ratio

items.q: Hafiz and Hui Min share $66 in the ratio 5 : 6. How much money does Hui Min get?
items.e: 5 + 6 = 11 units. 11 units = $66, so 1 unit = $66 ÷ 11 = $6. Hui Min gets 6 units: 6 × $6 = $36. Do not divide $66 by 6: find the total units first.

items.q: Arjun and Mei Ling share 35 marbles in the ratio 3 : 4. How many marbles does Mei Ling get?
items.e: 3 + 4 = 7 units. 7 units = 35 marbles, so 1 unit = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 marbles. Mei Ling gets 4 units: 4 × 5 marbles = 20 marbles. Do not divide 35 by 4: find the total units first.

items.q: The ratio of chicken wings to fish balls at a party is 8 : 3. There are 44 pieces altogether. How many more chicken wings than fish balls are there?
items.e: 1 unit = 44 ÷ 11 = 4. The difference is 8 − 3 = 5 units: 5 × 4 = 20. 5 is only the difference in the ratio, not the number of pieces.

items.q: Devi and Ahmad share 121 stickers in the ratio 7 : 4. How many stickers does Devi get?
items.e: 7 + 4 = 11 units. 11 units = 121 stickers, so 1 unit = 121 ÷ 11 = 11 stickers. Devi gets 7 units: 7 × 11 stickers = 77 stickers. Do not divide 121 by 7: find the total units first.

items.q: Mr Rahman pours 1 ℓ 500 ml of soya bean milk into a big jug and a small jug in the ratio 2 : 1. How much milk is in the big jug?
items.e: 1 ℓ 500 ml = 1500 ml. 2 + 1 = 3 units, so 1 unit = 1500 ÷ 3 = 500 ml. Big jug: 2 × 500 = 1000 ml. 750 ml shares the milk equally.

items.q: Jun Jie and Ryan share 165 stamps in the ratio 6 : 5. How many stamps does Jun Jie get?
items.e: 6 + 5 = 11 units. 11 units = 165 stamps, so 1 unit = 165 ÷ 11 = 15 stamps. Jun Jie gets 6 units: 6 × 15 stamps = 90 stamps. Do not divide 165 by 6: find the total units first.

items.q: Wei Ming and Kumar share some money in the ratio 4 : 5. What fraction of the money does Wei Ming get?
items.e: The whole is 4 + 5 = 9 units. Wei Ming gets 4 units out of 9: 49. 45 compares the two shares, not one share with the whole.

items.q: The ratio of the number of cats to the number of dogs in an animal shelter is 3 : 2. There are 30 animals. How many dogs are there?
items.e: 3 + 2 = 5 units. 5 units = 30, so 1 unit = 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Dogs: 2 × 6 = 12. 18 is the number of cats.

items.q: The ratio of red balloons to blue balloons at a Children’s Day party is 5 : 3. There are 32 balloons altogether. How many more red balloons than blue balloons are there?
items.e: 1 unit = 32 ÷ 8 = 4. The difference is 5 − 3 = 2 units: 2 × 4 = 8. 2 is only the difference in the ratio, not the number of balloons.

items.q: Farah and Kavya share 98 cards in the ratio 5 : 2. How many cards does Kavya get?
items.e: 5 + 2 = 7 units. 7 units = 98 cards, so 1 unit = 98 ÷ 7 = 14 cards. Kavya gets 2 units: 2 × 14 cards = 28 cards. Do not divide 98 by 2: find the total units first.

items.q: A 2.4 kg bag of nuts has peanuts and cashew nuts in the ratio 5 : 3 by mass. What is the mass of the cashew nuts?
items.e: 2.4 kg = 2400 g. 5 + 3 = 8 units, so 1 unit = 2400 ÷ 8 = 300 g. Cashew nuts: 3 × 300 = 900 g. 800 g is 2400 ÷ 3, which forgets the peanuts.

items.q: The ratio of the number of adults to the number of children in a hawker centre is 7 : 5. There are 84 people. How many children are there?
items.e: 7 + 5 = 12 units. 12 units = 84, so 1 unit = 84 ÷ 12 = 7. Children: 5 × 7 = 35. 49 is the number of adults.

items.q: Raju and Ethan share $75 in the ratio 2 : 3. How much money does Raju get?
items.e: 2 + 3 = 5 units. 5 units = $75, so 1 unit = $75 ÷ 5 = $15. Raju gets 2 units: 2 × $15 = $30. Do not divide $75 by 2: find the total units first.

items.q: The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a CCA is 2 : 9. There are 99 pupils. How many girls are there?
items.e: 2 + 9 = 11 units. 11 units = 99, so 1 unit = 99 ÷ 11 = 9. Girls: 9 × 9 = 81. 18 is the number of boys.

items.q: Xin Yi and Priya share $28 in the ratio 4 : 3. How much money does Xin Yi get?
items.e: 4 + 3 = 7 units. 7 units = $28, so 1 unit = $28 ÷ 7 = $4. Xin Yi gets 4 units: 4 × $4 = $16. Do not divide $28 by 4: find the total units first.

items.q: Zhi Hao and Chloe share $36 in the ratio 5 : 4. How much money does Chloe get?
items.e: 5 + 4 = 9 units. 9 units = $36, so 1 unit = $36 ÷ 9 = $4. Chloe gets 4 units: 4 × $4 = $16. Do not divide $36 by 4: find the total units first.

items.q: The ratio of girls to boys in a choir is 7 : 3. There are 70 pupils altogether. How many more girls than boys are there?
items.e: 1 unit = 70 ÷ 10 = 7. The difference is 7 − 3 = 4 units: 4 × 7 = 28. 4 is only the difference in the ratio, not the number of pupils.

items.q: A ribbon 3 m long is cut into two pieces in the ratio 2 : 3. How long is the shorter piece?
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. 2 + 3 = 5 units, so 1 unit = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 cm. Shorter piece: 2 × 60 = 120 cm. Do not divide 300 by 2 or by 3.

items.q: Ali and Sarah share some money in the ratio 4 : 7. What fraction of the money does Sarah get?
items.e: The whole is 4 + 7 = 11 units. Sarah gets 7 units out of 11: 711. 74 compares the two shares, not one share with the whole.

items.q: Mrs Lim makes 2 ℓ of lime juice. She mixes lime syrup and water in the ratio 1 : 4. How much water does she use?
items.e: 2 ℓ = 2000 ml. 1 + 4 = 5 units, so 1 unit = 2000 ÷ 5 = 400 ml. Water: 4 × 400 = 1600 ml. 400 ml is the syrup.

sets.title: Finding the other part or the total

items.q: The ratio of Xin Yi’s money to Priya’s money is 5 : 7. Xin Yi has $65. How much money does Priya have?
items.e: Xin Yi has 5 units = $65, so 1 unit = $65 ÷ 5 = $13. Priya has 7 units: 7 × $13 = $91. Do not just add 2 to $65: a ratio is about multiplying and dividing.

items.q: A box has red beads and yellow beads. 512 of the beads are red. What is the ratio of yellow beads to red beads?
items.e: Red is 5 units, so yellow is 12 − 5 = 7 units. Yellow : red = 7 : 5. Yellow is named first, so it goes first.

items.q: Jun Jie and Ryan share some cards in the ratio 7 : 6. Jun Jie gets 63 cards. How many cards do they share?
items.e: 7 units = 63 cards, so 1 unit = 9 cards. The total is 7 + 6 = 13 units: 13 × 9 cards = 117 cards. 54 cards is only Ryan’s share.

items.q: The ratio of Raju’s money to Ethan’s money is 3 : 5. Raju has $27. How much money does Ethan have?
items.e: Raju has 3 units = $27, so 1 unit = $27 ÷ 3 = $9. Ethan has 5 units: 5 × $9 = $45. Do not just add 2 to $27: a ratio is about multiplying and dividing.

items.q: Raju’s height is 45 of Kumar’s height. What is the ratio of Raju’s height to Kumar’s height?
items.e: If Kumar’s height is 5 units, then Raju’s height is 4 units. So the ratio is 4 : 5. 5 : 4 is the wrong way round.

items.q: Xin Yi has 45 stamps and Priya has 60 stamps. What is the ratio of Xin Yi’s stamps to the total number of stamps in its simplest form?
items.e: The total is 45 + 60 = 105, so the ratio is 45 : 105. The highest common factor is 15. Divide both numbers by 15: 3 : 7. 9 : 21 is equal in value, but it is not accepted: the question asks for the simplest form, and both numbers can still be divided by 3.

items.q: Ali’s savings are 35 of Siti’s savings. What is the ratio of Ali’s savings to Siti’s savings?
items.e: If Siti’s savings are 5 units, then Ali’s savings are 3 units. So the ratio is 3 : 5. 5 : 3 is the wrong way round.

items.q: The ratio of Devi’s seashells to Ahmad’s seashells is 2 : 7. Devi has 30 seashells. How many seashells does Ahmad have?
items.e: Devi has 2 units = 30 seashells, so 1 unit = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 seashells. Ahmad has 7 units: 7 × 15 seashells = 105 seashells. Do not just add 5 to 30: a ratio is about multiplying and dividing.

items.q: Siti and Nurul share some storybooks in the ratio 5 : 8. Siti gets 30 storybooks. How many storybooks do they share?
items.e: 5 units = 30 storybooks, so 1 unit = 6 storybooks. The total is 5 + 8 = 13 units: 13 × 6 storybooks = 78 storybooks. 48 storybooks is only Nurul’s share.

items.q: Raju and Ethan share some money in the ratio 5 : 6. Raju gets $30. How much money do they share?
items.e: 5 units = $30, so 1 unit = $6. The total is 5 + 6 = 11 units: 11 × $6 = $66. $36 is only Ethan’s share.

items.q: The ratio of Zhi Hao’s money to Chloe’s money is 4 : 7. Zhi Hao has $44. How much money does Chloe have?
items.e: Zhi Hao has 4 units = $44, so 1 unit = $44 ÷ 4 = $11. Chloe has 7 units: 7 × $11 = $77. Do not just add 3 to $44: a ratio is about multiplying and dividing.

items.q: The ratio of Hafiz’s beads to Hui Min’s beads is 4 : 9. Hafiz has 16 beads. How many beads does Hui Min have?
items.e: Hafiz has 4 units = 16 beads, so 1 unit = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 beads. Hui Min has 9 units: 9 × 4 beads = 36 beads. Do not just add 5 to 16: a ratio is about multiplying and dividing.

items.q: The ratio of Siti’s money to Nurul’s money is 2 : 5. Siti has $8. How much money does Nurul have?
items.e: Siti has 2 units = $8, so 1 unit = $8 ÷ 2 = $4. Nurul has 5 units: 5 × $4 = $20. Do not just add 3 to $8: a ratio is about multiplying and dividing.

items.q: In a class, 38 of the pupils are boys. What is the ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls?
items.e: Out of 8 units, 3 units are boys and 8 − 3 = 5 units are girls. Boys : girls = 3 : 5. 3 : 8 compares boys with the whole class.

items.q: Ali and Sarah share some money in the ratio 5 : 4. Ali gets $40. How much money do they share?
items.e: 5 units = $40, so 1 unit = $8. The total is 5 + 4 = 9 units: 9 × $8 = $72. $32 is only Sarah’s share.

items.q: Wei Ming and Kumar share some seashells in the ratio 7 : 3. Wei Ming gets 56 seashells. How many seashells do they share?
items.e: 7 units = 56 seashells, so 1 unit = 8 seashells. The total is 7 + 3 = 10 units: 10 × 8 seashells = 80 seashells. 24 seashells is only Kumar’s share.

items.q: Mdm Wong mixes 560 ml of apple juice with 420 ml of orange juice. What is the ratio of the volume of orange juice to the volume of apple juice in its simplest form?
items.e: The highest common factor is 140. Divide both numbers by 140: 3 : 4. 6 : 8 is equal in value, but it is not accepted: the question asks for the simplest form, and both numbers can still be divided by 2.

items.q: Zhi Hao has $24 and Chloe has $36. What is the ratio of Zhi Hao’s money to Chloe’s money in its simplest form?
items.e: The highest common factor is 12. Divide both numbers by 12: 2 : 3. 4 : 6 is equal in value, but it is not accepted: the question asks for the simplest form, and both numbers can still be divided by 2.

items.q: Farah and Kavya share some money in the ratio 8 : 3. Farah gets $64. How much money do they share?
items.e: 8 units = $64, so 1 unit = $8. The total is 8 + 3 = 11 units: 11 × $8 = $88. $24 is only Kavya’s share.

items.q: The ratio of Arjun’s erasers to Mei Ling’s erasers is 9 : 4. Arjun has 63 erasers. How many erasers does Mei Ling have?
items.e: Arjun has 9 units = 63 erasers, so 1 unit = 63 ÷ 9 = 7 erasers. Mei Ling has 4 units: 4 × 7 erasers = 28 erasers. Do not just take 5 from 63: a ratio is about multiplying and dividing.

items.q: The ratio of Arjun’s marbles to Mei Ling’s marbles is 5 : 2. Arjun has 33 more marbles than Mei Ling. How many marbles does Arjun have?
items.e: The difference is 5 − 2 = 3 units. 3 units = 33 marbles, so 1 unit = 33 ÷ 3 = 11 marbles. Arjun: 5 units = 5 × 11 marbles = 55 marbles. The difference is 3 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Hafiz’s stamps to Hui Min’s stamps is 7 : 5. Hafiz has 26 more stamps than Hui Min. How many stamps does Hui Min have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 5 = 2 units. 2 units = 26 stamps, so 1 unit = 26 ÷ 2 = 13 stamps. Hui Min: 5 units = 5 × 13 stamps = 65 stamps. The difference is 2 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Wei Ming’s money to Kumar’s money is 3 : 8. Wei Ming has $50 less than Kumar. How much money does Wei Ming have?
items.e: The difference is 8 − 3 = 5 units. 5 units = $50, so 1 unit = $50 ÷ 5 = $10. Wei Ming: 3 units = 3 × $10 = $30. The difference is 5 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Siti’s money to Nurul’s money is 2 : 5. Nurul has $12 more than Siti. How much money does Nurul have?
items.e: The difference is 5 − 2 = 3 units. 3 units = $12, so 1 unit = $12 ÷ 3 = $4. Nurul: 5 units = 5 × $4 = $20. The difference is 3 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Zhi Hao’s cards to Chloe’s cards is 5 : 7. Zhi Hao has 28 fewer cards than Chloe. How many cards does Chloe have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 5 = 2 units. 2 units = 28 cards, so 1 unit = 28 ÷ 2 = 14 cards. Chloe: 7 units = 7 × 14 cards = 98 cards. The difference is 2 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Jun Jie’s seashells to Ryan’s seashells is 4 : 7. Ryan has 9 more seashells than Jun Jie. How many seashells does Jun Jie have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 4 = 3 units. 3 units = 9 seashells, so 1 unit = 9 ÷ 3 = 3 seashells. Jun Jie: 4 units = 4 × 3 seashells = 12 seashells. The difference is 3 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Raju’s money to Ethan’s money is 7 : 4. Raju has $27 more than Ethan. How much money does Ethan have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 4 = 3 units. 3 units = $27, so 1 unit = $27 ÷ 3 = $9. Ethan: 4 units = 4 × $9 = $36. The difference is 3 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Ali’s stickers to Sarah’s stickers is 2 : 7. Sarah has 70 more stickers than Ali. How many stickers does Sarah have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 2 = 5 units. 5 units = 70 stickers, so 1 unit = 70 ÷ 5 = 14 stickers. Sarah: 7 units = 7 × 14 stickers = 98 stickers. The difference is 5 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Ali’s seashells to Sarah’s seashells is 3 : 7. Sarah has 32 more seashells than Ali. How many seashells does Ali have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 3 = 4 units. 4 units = 32 seashells, so 1 unit = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 seashells. Ali: 3 units = 3 × 8 seashells = 24 seashells. The difference is 4 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Farah’s money to Kavya’s money is 3 : 5. Farah has $22 less than Kavya. How much money does Farah have?
items.e: The difference is 5 − 3 = 2 units. 2 units = $22, so 1 unit = $22 ÷ 2 = $11. Farah: 3 units = 3 × $11 = $33. The difference is 2 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Raju’s storybooks to Ethan’s storybooks is 9 : 2. Ethan has 49 fewer storybooks than Raju. How many storybooks do they have altogether?
items.e: The difference is 9 − 2 = 7 units. 7 units = 49 storybooks, so 1 unit = 49 ÷ 7 = 7 storybooks. Altogether: 9 + 2 = 11 units = 11 × 7 storybooks = 77 storybooks. The difference is 7 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Arjun’s money to Mei Ling’s money is 4 : 9. Mei Ling has $45 more than Arjun. How much money do they have altogether?
items.e: The difference is 9 − 4 = 5 units. 5 units = $45, so 1 unit = $45 ÷ 5 = $9. Altogether: 4 + 9 = 13 units = 13 × $9 = $117. The difference is 5 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Wei Ming’s beads to Kumar’s beads is 5 : 8. Kumar has 33 more beads than Wei Ming. How many beads does Kumar have?
items.e: The difference is 8 − 5 = 3 units. 3 units = 33 beads, so 1 unit = 33 ÷ 3 = 11 beads. Kumar: 8 units = 8 × 11 beads = 88 beads. The difference is 3 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Devi’s money to Ahmad’s money is 7 : 3. Devi has $24 more than Ahmad. How much money does Ahmad have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 3 = 4 units. 4 units = $24, so 1 unit = $24 ÷ 4 = $6. Ahmad: 3 units = 3 × $6 = $18. The difference is 4 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Zhi Hao’s stickers to Chloe’s stickers is 8 : 5. Zhi Hao has 39 more stickers than Chloe. How many stickers does Chloe have?
items.e: The difference is 8 − 5 = 3 units. 3 units = 39 stickers, so 1 unit = 39 ÷ 3 = 13 stickers. Chloe: 5 units = 5 × 13 stickers = 65 stickers. The difference is 3 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Devi’s cards to Ahmad’s cards is 9 : 4. Ahmad has 65 fewer cards than Devi. How many cards does Devi have?
items.e: The difference is 9 − 4 = 5 units. 5 units = 65 cards, so 1 unit = 65 ÷ 5 = 13 cards. Devi: 9 units = 9 × 13 cards = 117 cards. The difference is 5 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Farah’s erasers to Kavya’s erasers is 8 : 3. Farah has 15 more erasers than Kavya. How many erasers does Farah have?
items.e: The difference is 8 − 3 = 5 units. 5 units = 15 erasers, so 1 unit = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 erasers. Farah: 8 units = 8 × 3 erasers = 24 erasers. The difference is 5 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Siti’s marbles to Nurul’s marbles is 2 : 9. Nurul has 35 more marbles than Siti. How many marbles do they have altogether?
items.e: The difference is 9 − 2 = 7 units. 7 units = 35 marbles, so 1 unit = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 marbles. Altogether: 2 + 9 = 11 units = 11 × 5 marbles = 55 marbles. The difference is 7 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Jun Jie’s stamps to Ryan’s stamps is 5 : 3. Jun Jie has 10 more stamps than Ryan. How many stamps do they have altogether?
items.e: The difference is 5 − 3 = 2 units. 2 units = 10 stamps, so 1 unit = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 stamps. Altogether: 5 + 3 = 8 units = 8 × 5 stamps = 40 stamps. The difference is 2 units, not 1 unit.

items.q: The ratio of Xin Yi’s money to Priya’s money is 7 : 2. Xin Yi has $50 more than Priya. How much money does Xin Yi have?
items.e: The difference is 7 − 2 = 5 units. 5 units = $50, so 1 unit = $50 ÷ 5 = $10. Xin Yi: 7 units = 7 × $10 = $70. The difference is 5 units, not 1 unit.

sets.title: Before and after: same total, same difference or one part unchanged

items.q: The ratio of Priya’s cards to Hafiz’s cards was 5 : 4. After Priya gave Hafiz 16 cards, the ratio became 1 : 2. How many cards does Hafiz have now?
items.e: The total does not change, so give both ratios the same total. Before: 5 : 4 (9 units). After: 1 : 2 = 3 : 6 (9 units). Priya went from 5 units to 3 units, so Priya gave away 2 units. 2 units = 16, so 1 unit = 8. Hafiz now: 6 units = 48 cards. Do not compare 5 : 4 and 1 : 2 as they are: their totals are 9 and 3 units.

items.q: The ratio of Farah’s money to Kavya’s money was 2 : 3. They each spent $36 at a book fair. Then the ratio became 2 : 5. How much money does Kavya have now?
items.e: They spent the same amount, so the difference between them does not change. Give the difference the same number of units. Before: 2 : 3 = 6 : 9 (difference 3 units). After: 2 : 5 (difference 3 units). Farah’s money went down from 6 units to 2 units, that is 4 units. 4 units = $36, so 1 unit = $9. Kavya now: 5 units = $45. Do not compare 2 : 3 and 2 : 5 as they are: their differences are 1 and 3 units.

items.q: The ratio of the number of adults to the number of children in a hall was 3 : 8. After 20 adults left the hall, the ratio became 1 : 8. How many children were in the hall?
items.e: The number of children does not change, and it is 8 units in both ratios. The number of adults went from 3 units to 1 unit, a change of 2 units. 2 units = 20, so 1 unit = 10. Children: 8 units = 80 children.

items.q: The ratio of Priya’s money to Hafiz’s money was 4 : 7. After Priya spent $22, the ratio became 2 : 7. How much money did Priya have at first?
items.e: Hafiz’s money does not change, and it is 7 units in both ratios. Priya’s money went from 4 units to 2 units, a change of 2 units. 2 units = $22, so 1 unit = $11. Priya at first: 4 units = $44.

items.q: The ratio of Jun Jie’s storybooks to Ryan’s storybooks was 2 : 1. After Jun Jie gave away 35 storybooks, the ratio became 7 : 6. How many storybooks did they have altogether at first?
items.e: Ryan’s storybooks do not change, so use the same number of units for Ryan in both ratios. Before: 2 : 1 = 12 : 6. After: 7 : 6. Jun Jie’s storybooks went from 12 units to 7 units, a change of 5 units. 5 units = 35, so 1 unit = 7. Altogether at first: 18 units = 126 storybooks. Do not compare 2 : 1 and 7 : 6 as they are: Ryan has 1 unit in one and 6 units in the other.

items.q: The ratio of Sarah’s storybooks to Siti’s storybooks was 9 : 1. After Sarah gave Siti 50 storybooks, the ratio became 2 : 3. How many storybooks does Siti have now?
items.e: The total does not change, so give both ratios the same total. Before: 9 : 1 (10 units). After: 2 : 3 = 4 : 6 (10 units). Sarah went from 9 units to 4 units, so Sarah gave away 5 units. 5 units = 50, so 1 unit = 10. Siti now: 6 units = 60 storybooks. Do not compare 9 : 1 and 2 : 3 as they are: their totals are 10 and 5 units.

items.q: The ratio of Devi’s money to Ahmad’s money was 2 : 7. They each spent $5 at a book fair. Then the ratio became 1 : 6. How much money did Ahmad have at first?
items.e: They spent the same amount, so the difference between them does not change. The difference is 5 units in both ratios. Devi’s money went down from 2 units to 1 unit, that is 1 unit. 1 unit = $5. Ahmad at first: 7 units = $35.

items.q: The ratio of Arjun’s money to Mei Ling’s money was 1 : 2. After Arjun’s grandmother gave him $21, the ratio became 5 : 4. How much money did Arjun have at first?
items.e: Mei Ling’s money does not change, so use the same number of units for Mei Ling in both ratios. Before: 1 : 2 = 2 : 4. After: 5 : 4. Arjun’s money went from 2 units to 5 units, a change of 3 units. 3 units = $21, so 1 unit = $7. Arjun at first: 2 units = $14. Do not compare 1 : 2 and 5 : 4 as they are: Mei Ling has 2 units in one and 4 units in the other.

items.q: The ratio of Kavya’s seashells to Wei Ming’s seashells was 7 : 4. After Kavya gave Wei Ming 24 seashells, the ratio became 4 : 7. How many seashells did Kavya have at first?
items.e: The total does not change: 7 : 4 and 4 : 7 both have 11 units. Kavya went from 7 units to 4 units, so Kavya gave away 3 units. 3 units = 24, so 1 unit = 8. Kavya at first: 7 units = 56 seashells.

items.q: The ratio of Hui Min’s age to Mr Tan’s age is 1 : 7 now. In 15 years’ time, the ratio will be 2 : 5. How old is Hui Min now?
items.e: Both people get 15 years older, so the difference in their ages does not change. Give the difference the same number of units. Before: 1 : 7 (difference 6 units). After: 2 : 5 = 4 : 10 (difference 6 units). Hui Min’s age went up from 1 unit to 4 units, that is 3 units. 3 units = 15 years, so 1 unit = 5 years. Hui Min now: 1 unit = 5 years old. Do not compare 1 : 7 and 2 : 5 as they are: their differences are 6 and 3 units.

items.q: The ratio of Hui Min’s beads to Devi’s beads was 4 : 9. After Hui Min bought 22 more beads, the ratio became 2 : 3. How many beads did they have altogether at first?
items.e: Devi’s beads do not change, so use the same number of units for Devi in both ratios. Before: 4 : 9. After: 2 : 3 = 6 : 9. Hui Min’s beads went from 4 units to 6 units, a change of 2 units. 2 units = 22, so 1 unit = 11. Altogether at first: 13 units = 143 beads. Do not compare 4 : 9 and 2 : 3 as they are: Devi has 9 units in one and 3 units in the other.

items.q: The ratio of Ethan’s marbles to Zhi Hao’s marbles was 4 : 1. After Ethan gave Zhi Hao 35 marbles, the ratio became 3 : 7. How many marbles did Ethan have at first?
items.e: The total does not change, so give both ratios the same total. Before: 4 : 1 = 8 : 2 (10 units). After: 3 : 7 (10 units). Ethan went from 8 units to 3 units, so Ethan gave away 5 units. 5 units = 35, so 1 unit = 7. Ethan at first: 8 units = 56 marbles. Do not compare 4 : 1 and 3 : 7 as they are: their totals are 5 and 10 units.

items.q: The ratio of the volume of water in Tank A to the volume of water in Tank B was 3 : 2. After 42 ℓ of water was poured from Tank A into Tank B, the ratio became 3 : 7. How much water was in Tank A at first?
items.e: The total does not change, so give both ratios the same total. Before: 3 : 2 = 6 : 4 (10 units). After: 3 : 7 (10 units). Tank A went from 6 units to 3 units, so Tank A gave away 3 units. 3 units = 42 ℓ, so 1 unit = 14 ℓ. Tank A at first: 6 units = 84 ℓ. Do not compare 3 : 2 and 3 : 7 as they are: their totals are 5 and 10 units.

items.q: The ratio of Ryan’s age to Mrs Ng’s age is 1 : 4 now. In 18 years’ time, the ratio will be 1 : 2. How old will Mrs Ng be in 18 years’ time?
items.e: Both people get 18 years older, so the difference in their ages does not change. Give the difference the same number of units. Before: 1 : 4 (difference 3 units). After: 1 : 2 = 3 : 6 (difference 3 units). Ryan’s age went up from 1 unit to 3 units, that is 2 units. 2 units = 18 years, so 1 unit = 9 years. Mrs Ng then: 6 units = 54 years old. Do not compare 1 : 4 and 1 : 2 as they are: their differences are 3 and 1 units.

items.q: The ratio of Arjun’s age to Mrs Lim’s age is 1 : 5 now. In 7 years’ time, the ratio will be 1 : 3. How old is Mrs Lim now?
items.e: Both people get 7 years older, so the difference in their ages does not change. Give the difference the same number of units. Before: 1 : 5 (difference 4 units). After: 1 : 3 = 2 : 6 (difference 4 units). Arjun’s age went up from 1 unit to 2 units, that is 1 unit. 1 unit = 7 years. Mrs Lim now: 5 units = 35 years old. Do not compare 1 : 5 and 1 : 3 as they are: their differences are 4 and 2 units.

items.q: The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a hall was 2 : 9. After 12 more boys came into the hall, the ratio became 1 : 3. How many girls were in the hall?
items.e: The number of girls does not change, so use the same number of units for the girls in both ratios. Before: 2 : 9. After: 1 : 3 = 3 : 9. The number of boys went from 2 units to 3 units, a change of 1 unit. 1 unit = 12. Girls: 9 units = 108 girls. Do not compare 2 : 9 and 1 : 3 as they are: the girls are 9 units in one and 3 units in the other.

items.q: The ratio of Mei Ling’s savings to Jun Jie’s savings was 1 : 9. They each saved another $50. Then the ratio became 3 : 7. How much did Mei Ling have in savings at first?
items.e: They saved the same amount, so the difference between them does not change. Give the difference the same number of units. Before: 1 : 9 (difference 8 units). After: 3 : 7 = 6 : 14 (difference 8 units). Mei Ling’s savings went up from 1 unit to 6 units, that is 5 units. 5 units = $50, so 1 unit = $10. Mei Ling at first: 1 unit = $10. Do not compare 1 : 9 and 3 : 7 as they are: their differences are 8 and 4 units.

items.q: The ratio of Kumar’s money to Ali’s money was 5 : 4. After Kumar gave Ali $24, the ratio became 2 : 7. How much money does Ali have now?
items.e: The total does not change: 5 : 4 and 2 : 7 both have 9 units. Kumar went from 5 units to 2 units, so Kumar gave away 3 units. 3 units = $24, so 1 unit = $8. Ali now: 7 units = $56.

items.q: The ratio of the number of adults to the number of children in a hall was 7 : 4. After 10 adults left the hall, the ratio became 3 : 2. How many children were in the hall?
items.e: The number of children does not change, so use the same number of units for the children in both ratios. Before: 7 : 4. After: 3 : 2 = 6 : 4. The number of adults went from 7 units to 6 units, a change of 1 unit. 1 unit = 10. Children: 4 units = 40 children. Do not compare 7 : 4 and 3 : 2 as they are: the children are 4 units in one and 2 units in the other.

items.q: The ratio of Chloe’s money to Xin Yi’s money was 2 : 1. After Chloe gave Xin Yi $18, the ratio became 5 : 7. How much money do they have altogether?
items.e: The total does not change, so give both ratios the same total. Before: 2 : 1 = 8 : 4 (12 units). After: 5 : 7 (12 units). Chloe went from 8 units to 5 units, so Chloe gave away 3 units. 3 units = $18, so 1 unit = $6. Altogether: 12 units = $72. Do not compare 2 : 1 and 5 : 7 as they are: their totals are 3 and 12 units.

items.q: The ratio of Hui Min’s stickers to Devi’s stickers was 2 : 5. Hui Min bought 6 more stickers and Devi gave away 18 stickers. Then they had the same number of stickers. How many stickers did Hui Min have at first?
items.e: 2 units + 6 = 5 units − 18. So 3 units = 6 + 18 = 24 and 1 unit = 8. Hui Min at first: 2 × 8 = 16 stickers. Check: 16 + 6 = 22 and 40 − 18 = 22.

items.q: The ratio of Sarah’s money to Siti’s money is 2 : 3. The ratio of Siti’s money to Nurul’s money is 4 : 5. They have $350 altogether. How much money does Nurul have?
items.e: Make Siti’s units the same: 2 : 3 = 8 : 12 and 4 : 5 = 12 : 15. So Sarah : Siti : Nurul = 8 : 12 : 15 = 35 units. 1 unit = $350 ÷ 35 = $10. Nurul: 15 × $10 = $150. $175 comes from 2 : 3 : 5, which joins ratios where Siti’s units are different.

items.q: The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a choir was 3 : 4. After 14 boys left the choir, the ratio became 1 : 2. How many boys were in the choir at first?
items.e: The number of girls does not change. Make the girls the same: 3 : 4 and 1 : 2 = 2 : 4. Boys went from 3 units to 2 units, so 1 unit = 14. Boys at first: 3 × 14 = 42. 21 comes from 3 − 1 = 2 units, which changes the girls’ units.

items.q: At a magic show, the ratio of adults to children was 2 : 5. After 30 children left, the ratio became 4 : 7. How many people were at the show at first?
items.e: The number of adults does not change. Make the adults the same: 2 : 5 = 4 : 10, and after it is 4 : 7. Children went from 10 units to 7 units: 3 units = 30, so 1 unit = 10. At first: 4 + 10 = 14 units = 140 people. 110 is the number of people after.

items.q: The ratio of Ryan’s cards to Farah’s cards was 7 : 5. After Ryan gave Farah 9 cards, they had the same number of cards. How many cards did they have altogether?
items.e: The total stays the same. 7 : 5 is 12 units. After, they are equal: 6 units each. Ryan gave 7 − 6 = 1 unit, so 1 unit = 9. Total: 12 × 9 = 108 cards. 63 is what Ryan had at first.

items.q: Ethan and Zhi Hao had 120 marbles altogether in the ratio 5 : 3. Ethan gave some marbles to Zhi Hao. Then the ratio became 3 : 5. How many marbles did Ethan give to Zhi Hao?
items.e: The total stays 8 units. 8 units = 120, so 1 unit = 15. Ethan went from 5 units to 3 units, so Ethan gave 2 units = 2 × 15 = 30 marbles.

items.q: Chloe had $80 and Xin Yi had $50. They each spent the same amount of money. Then the ratio of Chloe’s money to Xin Yi’s money became 5 : 2. How much money did each of them spend?
items.e: The difference stays $80 − $50 = $30. After: 5 − 2 = 3 units = $30, so 1 unit = $10. Chloe has 5 units = $50 left. Each spent $80 − $50 = $30.

items.q: At a fruit stall, the ratio of apples to oranges is 3 : 2. The ratio of oranges to pears is 5 : 4. There are 42 more apples than pears. How many oranges are there?
items.e: Make the oranges the same: 3 : 2 = 15 : 10 and 5 : 4 = 10 : 8. Apples : oranges : pears = 15 : 10 : 8. Apples − pears = 7 units = 42, so 1 unit = 6. Oranges: 10 × 6 = 60. 90 is the number of apples.

items.q: Mdm Wong is 40 years old. Her son, Hafiz, is 10 years old. In how many years will the ratio of Mdm Wong’s age to Hafiz’s age be 5 : 2?
items.e: The difference in age never changes: 40 − 10 = 30 years. 5 − 2 = 3 units = 30 years, so 1 unit = 10 years. Hafiz will be 2 units = 20 years old, which is in 20 − 10 = 10 years. 20 is his age then.

items.q: The ratio of the volume of water in Tank A to the volume of water in Tank B is 3 : 1. After 12 ℓ of water is poured from Tank A into Tank B, both tanks have the same volume of water. How much water was in Tank A at first?
items.e: 4 units in all, so each tank ends with 2 units. Tank A gives 3 − 2 = 1 unit = 12 ℓ. Tank A at first: 3 × 12 = 36 ℓ. 24 ℓ is the volume in each tank after.

items.q: 25 of Mei Ling’s beads is equal to 13 of Jun Jie’s beads. They have 132 beads altogether. How many beads does Jun Jie have?
items.e: 13 = 26, so Mei Ling has 5 units and Jun Jie has 6 units. 11 units = 132, so 1 unit = 12. Jun Jie: 6 × 12 = 72. Check: 25 of 60 = 24 and 13 of 72 = 24.

items.q: Raju spent 14 of his money on a book and 25 of the remainder on a bag. What is the ratio of the money spent on the bag to the money he had left?
items.e: Let his money be 20 units. Book: 5 units. Remainder: 15 units. Bag: 25 of 15 = 6 units. Left: 15 − 6 = 9 units. Bag : left = 6 : 9 = 2 : 3.

items.q: Mr Tan has some $5 notes and $10 notes in the ratio 3 : 2. The total value of the notes is $280. How many $10 notes does he have?
items.e: 1 group = 3 notes of $5 and 2 notes of $10 = $15 + $20 = $35. $280 ÷ $35 = 8 groups. $10 notes: 8 × 2 = 16. 24 is the number of $5 notes.

items.q: 23 of Ahmad’s marbles is equal to 12 of Arjun’s marbles. What is the ratio of Ahmad’s marbles to Arjun’s marbles?
items.e: Make the numerators the same: 12 = 24. So 2 units are 23 of Ahmad’s marbles and 24 of Arjun’s marbles. Ahmad has 3 units and Arjun has 4 units: 3 : 4. 4 : 3 is the wrong way round.

items.q: The ratio of Kavya’s stamps to Wei Ming’s stamps was 5 : 3. After Kavya gave Wei Ming 21 stamps, the ratio became 1 : 3. How many stamps did Wei Ming have at first?
items.e: The total does not change. 5 : 3 has 8 units and 1 : 3 has 4 units, so make it 2 : 6 (8 units). Kavya went from 5 units to 2 units: 3 units = 21, so 1 unit = 7. Wei Ming at first: 3 × 7 = 21 stamps. 42 is the number Wei Ming has now.

items.q: The ratio of the price of a pen to the price of a file is 2 : 3. Siti paid $12 for 3 pens and 2 files. How much does one file cost?
items.e: 1 pen = 2 units and 1 file = 3 units. 3 pens + 2 files = 6 units + 6 units = 12 units = $12, so 1 unit = $1. 1 file: 3 units = $3. $7.20 shares $12 in the ratio 2 : 3, which ignores how many of each were bought.

items.q: A box has red, blue and green beads in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7. There are 24 more green beads than red beads. How many beads are there in the box?
items.e: Green − red = 7 − 3 = 4 units. 4 units = 24, so 1 unit = 6. Total: 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 units = 15 × 6 = 90 beads. 360 treats the difference 24 as 1 unit.

items.q: A baker mixes flour, sugar and butter in the ratio 4 : 1 : 3 by mass. She uses 450 g of butter. How much flour does she use?
items.e: Butter: 3 units = 450 g, so 1 unit = 150 g. Flour: 4 units = 4 × 150 = 600 g. 1800 g is 450 × 4, which uses 450 g as 1 unit.

items.q: Kumar, Ali and Sarah shared some stickers in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. Then Sarah gave 15 of her stickers to Kumar. What is the new ratio of Kumar’s stickers to Ali’s stickers to Sarah’s stickers?
items.e: 15 of 5 units is 1 unit. Kumar: 2 + 1 = 3 units, Ali: 3 units, Sarah: 5 − 1 = 4 units. New ratio: 3 : 3 : 4. Remember to add the unit to Kumar too.

items.q: Wei Ming, Kumar and Ali shared $360 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How much money did Ali get?
items.e: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 units. 9 units = $360, so 1 unit = $40. Ali: 4 units = 4 × $40 = $160. $90 is $360 ÷ 4, which forgets the other two shares.
